title: Build: The Store MCP Server
objective: After this lesson you will be able to scaffold a version-pinned MCP server (TS SDK v2) with catalog/order tools, a policy resource, and a triage prompt — wired to serve over stdio with Inspector verification at every step.
why: Seven lessons of pieces; one lesson of assembly. The store server (catalog search, order lookup, gated refund, shipment tracking + policy resource + triage prompt) is the reference implementation every later pattern points at — and your capstone's starting fork. Build order matters: read-only first, gated money last, verification at each arrow.

blocks.text: Pin everything: `@modelcontextprotocol/server` (v2 line), `zod/v4`, Node 20+, `type: module` (ESM only), spec 2026-07-28 in the README. Pins convert 'works on my machine' into reproducible builds — and the Inspector version check (below) verifies the wire matches the pins.

blocks.caption: createServer factory: build testable, serve thin

blocks.text: Register reads before writes: `search-orders` (query + limit≤50), `lookup-order` (exact ID, outputSchema + structuredContent), policy `resource`, triage `prompt`. Verify each with the Inspector before adding the next — working reads prove transport, schemas, and discovery; money comes only on proven ground.

blocks.caption: Reads first with sibling descriptions and structured outputs

blocks.text: Money last: gated refund with the full stack

Refund arrives with everything: Zod schema (orderId pattern + amount bounds), idempotency key required, elicitation approval over thresholds, isError discipline, audit logging, stdout-clean handler. Gated money on proven read ground — never first, never ungated, never unlogged.

blocks.caption: Money tools carry keys, bounds, and approval references in-schema

blocks.text: Verify with Inspector at every arrow

The **MCP Inspector** connects to your server for interactive tools/list, tools/call with forms, resources/read, and prompt rendering — the fastest loop for schema mistakes (invalid args rejected visibly), description quality (would *you* pick correctly?), and transport health. Verify reads → resources/prompts → gated money, in that order; each green gate before the next arrow.

blocks.title: Order the build
blocks.note: Run it: expect 'order sound' then the violation naming money-before-reads. Build order is a dependency graph: reads prove ground that money requires.

items: Pin versions (SDK/zod/Node/spec) + createServer factory for testability
Reads → resources/prompts → Inspector-verified ground → gated money last
Money carries keys, bounds, approval refs in-schema; Inspector gates every arrow

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the practice ordering check on both orders and explain the violation. (b) Write the shipment-tracking tool spec (name/title/description with sibling sentence/schema/outputSchema) in v2 shape. (c) List the Inspector verifications per stage (reads, resource, prompt, refund) with what green means each time.
hints: Sound order vs money-first violation: reads prove transport/schemas/discovery that money requires.
Tracking tool mirrors lookup-order shape with tracking-number pattern + status outputSchema; sibling sentence vs order-status tools.
Inspector gates: tools/list shows all → call forms validate → resources read → refund path exercises approval → audit entries appear.
exercise.why: Build-order discipline (reads prove ground), spec authorship (new tool in house style), and Inspector gating (verify per arrow) are the three build judgments — each performed, not described.
exercise.code: // Build-order pattern: reads → verify → money; Inspector per arrow.

quiz.q: First tool to build on a greenfield MCP server?
options: A read-only lookup: proves transport, schemas, discovery with zero blast radius
quiz.explain: Reads prove ground money requires. Blast-radius ordering: reads → resources → gated writes, verified per arrow.

options: In-memory testing without transports: import, call tools directly, assert — transport is the thin last layer
quiz.explain: Testability by construction: factories separate build from serve. Transport wiring stays thin and late.

quiz.q: Inspector shows the refund tool but approval never triggers. Missing?
options: Elicitation wiring + approvalRef schema requirement: the gate path untested end to end — verify gated paths, not just listings
quiz.explain: Listings prove advertisement; gated paths need end-to-end exercise (elicit → verdict → execute/audit). Verify behavior, not presence.

summary: Pinned scaffold, reads first, Inspector per arrow, gated money last with keys and approval refs. Build order is dependency order with proof.
next: Built and green — now break it professionally: Inspector workflows, tracing, versions, and error codes. Next: debugging like an operator.
